institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 18, No. 1: percentage sensitivity, January to December 2011. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published April 2012.
reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus wound swab, body fluids, respiratory isolates), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in pie-chart legends and an "others" list.
method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2010 guidelines; repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses).

verification.note: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text, so the pages whose GNB columns are in a different order map correctly; OPD, ward and ICU taken from each row's background colour and checked against the row order), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences. Organism pie charts (no data labels): legend and "others" entries were parsed from the text layer, checked arithmetically per panel (legend counts plus Others equal the printed Isolates, "others" entries sum to Others; the one exception, respiratory ward, is a source inconsistency described in notes) and compared by eye with the rendered charts. Names split over two lines in the "others" lists were read from the image.

notes: Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 18, No. 1 (published April 2012), data January to December 2011, 8 pages; the older edition of the layout used in 2024. Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus wound swab; body fluids; respiratory isolates): organism pie charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, legend counts and an "others" list) and GPC and GNB percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus, sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)" is recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci. Combined columns: "Imipenem / Meropenem" (every GNB table) is recorded under meropenem and "Vancomycin/Teicoplanin" under vancomycin, each cell noted; the "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded; blood Salmonella also print nalidixic acid separately (recorded). The pus and body fluid GNB tables print cefoperazone-sulbactam before piperacillin-tazobactam; every table was mapped by its own headers. Blood S. pneumoniae OPD penicillin is printed "90*" with the footnote "1 isolate was moderately sensitive". Colistin and tigecycline are printed as percent susceptible for Enterobacterales and non-fermenters; no interpretive criteria are stated for them beyond "CLSI 2010". Isolate numbers: pus coagulase-negative staphylococci OPD (chart 87, table 82) and ward (chart 45, table 44) disagree; both recorded as printed and noted on the rows. The respiratory ward chart prints "Others - 54", but its "others" list sums to 43, and the legend plus 43 equals the printed 352 isolates. Several percentages cannot be produced by the row's n (per-drug tested numbers are not printed; for example pus ICU coagulase-negative staphylococci n=8, penicillin 11); recorded as printed. Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Serratia marscecens", "Morgnella", "Elizebethkingia", "S. maltophila", "Strept. viridans" as viridans group streptococci); "Salmonella typhimurium" is recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella; entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Fungal isolates are counted in the charts; their susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. The live URL no longer exists; the PDF was retrieved from the Wayback Machine copy https://web.archive.org/web/20120512183945id_/http://sgrh.com/newsletters/mb%20apr%202012.pdf and opens completely (8 pages, 428 KB, not truncated).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 1,217 cells (the seeded 25% sample of 304 from sample_cells.py, spread over all 10 GPC and GNB tables on pages 2 to 6, plus every other cell), all 120 row n values and all 269 organism counts were read from the page images (tables at scale 3 to 4 cut into halves with the row labels kept; pie legends and "others" lists at scale 5; the cells not kept and the count mismatches again at scale 8 to 10) before comparing with the extraction.

Result: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected (sample 0 of 304, whole file 0 of 1,217 cells, 0 of 120 n, 0 of 269 counts). OPD, ward and ICU correct on every row (yellow, blue and pink fills of the colour key, and every row n equals its OPD, ward or ICU pie legend entry apart from the two pus CoNS rows below); organism and specimen correct on every row (Pus wound swab as pus, Body fluids as sterile); every printed value of a recorded column is in the file, and the 9 table rows not recorded are exactly the 9 rows printed all "-", as excluded says. No table reached the 2% error threshold.

Combined columns: all 73 Imipenem/Meropenem cells (under meropenem) and all 42 Vancomycin/Teicoplanin cells (under vancomycin) carry their cell note. This edition has no Cefoxitin/Oxacillin column: all five GPC tables are headed Oxacillin alone and cefoxitin appears nowhere in the PDF, so the 24 oxacillin cells rightly carry no combined-column note. High Dose Gentamicin (9 Enterococcus cells) is recorded as gentamicin_hl; the Quinolones column is excluded, as notes say.

The 28 cells not kept (27 intrinsic, 1 caution) are all printed as recorded, none is a transcription error: blood S. pneumoniae gentamicin 0, 100, 0 (OPD, ward, ICU); Acinetobacter aztreonam blood 43, 25, 7, urine 8, 9 (OPD, ward), pus 7, 3, 0, body fluids 50, 0, 0 and respiratory 8, 0, 2; urine Proteus colistin 0, 0, 0; pus Proteus tigecycline 0, 0 and colistin 0, 0 (OPD, ward); respiratory Klebsiella ampicillin 0, 0, 1; caution: pus ICU CoNS penicillin 11 with n = 8 (conflict text accurate).

Count mismatches confirmed as printed (source inconsistency, already noted on the rows): pus CoNS OPD 87 in the pie legend against n = 82 in the GPC table, and ward 45 against 44. Each pus panel adds up to its printed Isolates total (778, 660) with 87 and 45, so the charts are internally consistent and the table n differs. Also confirmed: respiratory ward "Others - 54" against an others list that sums to 43 (legend plus 43 = the printed 352 isolates).

For readers of the counts: S. maltophilia is printed twice in the body fluids ICU and respiratory ICU panels ("S. maltophila" 1 and 3 beside "Stenotrophomonas maltophilia" 2 and 42); both entries are recorded as printed and the build sums them (3 and 45).

excluded.what: Quinolones column of every GPC and GNB table (pages 2 to 6)
excluded.why: drug class with no agent named, no canonical drug key

excluded.what: Rows printed with every drug not done ("-") or with no isolates
excluded.why: no values: blood Salmonella paratyphi A ICU (n=0), P. aeruginosa OPD (n=2); urine S. aureus ICU (n=0), Enterobacter ICU (n=6), Citrobacter ICU (n=3), Acinetobacter ICU (n=6); pus Proteus ICU (n=5); body fluids S. aureus ICU (n=2), Staphylococci spp. (CONS) ICU (n=3)

excluded.what: Page 7: prescription auditing of antimicrobials (DDD per 100 bed days, 2011) and the Drug Resistance Index chart (2009 to 2011)
excluded.why: antimicrobial consumption and a composite resistance index, not percent susceptible (the consumption bars carry no data labels)

excluded.what: Page 8: highlight based on blood isolates in IPD (ACCo in S. Typhi 5.9%; prevalence of ESBL, CRE, MRSA and VRE per blood cultures processed; MRSA isolation rate 57%; VRE 33.3%; CRE 6% to 60%)
excluded.why: phenotype summaries without organism-level denominators, not drug-level percent susceptible

excluded.what: Page 1: brucellosis case report and Table 1 (culture-proven brucellosis 2006 to 2011)
excluded.why: case report and serology, no susceptibility data

excluded.what: Organism count entries with no canonical organism key
excluded.why: not recordable: Fungal isolates (also printed "Fiungal", "Fungla"), Achromobacter spp., Chryseobacterium (printed "Chrysobacterium spp."), Ochrobactrum anthropi, Ralstonia pickettii, Ralstonia mannitolilytica, Brevundimonas spp., Pantoea spp., Myroides spp., Alcaligenes faecalis, Alcaligenes spp., Lactococcus spp., Nocardia spp., Trichosporon mucoides, Moraxella spp., Haemophilus spp., Streptococcus bovis, Pseudomonas putida, Pseudomonas stutzeri

excluded.what: Organism count entries that would add to the key of a tabulated organism
excluded.why: Pseudomonas spp. (also "Pseudomonas sps.", resolves to P. aeruginosa), Salmonella spp. (typhoidal Salmonella group, the parent of the S. Typhi and S. Paratyphi A rows), E coli variant (E. coli key): recording them would misstate the tabulated organism's isolate count
